requirement: The system shall import 3D image stacks from Nikon `.nd2`, Leica `.lif`, Zeiss `.czi`, and `.tif`/`.ome.tif` files.
activities: GOLD-IO reader tests; cross-platform install test

requirement: The system shall support multi-series containers (multiple positions or series in `.lif`/`.nd2`/`.czi`) and let the user select one, several, or all series.
The system shall support multichannel stacks and analyze each channel independently.
The system shall extract voxel size (x, y, z) from file metadata, plus objective NA, immersion refractive index, emission and excitation wavelength, pinhole size, and modality where available.
activities: Metadata resolver tests; GOLD-IO metadata fixtures

requirement: The system shall allow any metadata value to be entered or overridden manually, and shall record whether each value came from the file or from the user.
activities: Metadata resolver tests; GOLD-IO metadata fixtures

requirement: The system shall refuse to analyze a stack that lacks a required parameter (voxel size, NA, wavelength, RI) and shall report which parameter is missing.
activities: Metadata resolver tests; GOLD-IO metadata fixtures

requirement: The system shall support time-lapse or mosaic data by letting the user select timepoint or tile indices.
activities: Time/tile selection tests; large-file lazy-load test (memory cap)

requirement: The system shall handle stacks larger than RAM by lazy or chunked loading (e.g. dask).
activities: Time/tile selection tests; large-file lazy-load test (memory cap)

requirement: The system shall record a SHA-256 hash of each source file for provenance.

The system shall support instrument profiles (microscope, objective, channel presets) that supply default metadata, including values no file records such as bead diameter and the bead dye's emission peak, and link results to a tracked configuration.
activities: Profile schema validation; profile → session linking

requirement: The system shall automatically detect candidate beads in a 3D field (e.g. by LoG or DoG filtering followed by local maxima detection).
The system shall reject beads that are too close to the image border in xy or z for the configured crop size.
The system shall reject beads whose crop region overlaps another bead (minimum separation configurable, default ≥ 4× expected lateral FWHM laterally and ≥ 2× axial FWHM).
The system shall reject saturated beads (any voxel at the bit-depth maximum or at a configured threshold).
The system shall reject beads with SNR or SBR below configured thresholds.
The system shall reject outliers (e.g. aggregates or doublets) by integrated-intensity and FWHM outlier tests (median ± k·MAD).
The system shall let the user manually include or exclude beads in the GUI.
The system shall report the number of detected, rejected (with reason), and accepted beads.
**FWHM X, Y, Z** from 1D Gaussian fits (with offset) to line profiles through the sub-pixel bead centroid.
**FWHM in the XY, XZ, and YZ planes** from 2D Gaussian fits to the central orthogonal slices (or max projections, configurable). Reports major and minor axis FWHM and orientation angle.
**3D Gaussian fit** reporting FWHM x/y/z and the sub-pixel centroid.

**Integrated intensity (integrated density)**: background-subtracted sum within a defined volume (ellipsoid scaled to k × FWHM, or a fixed box), reported in raw counts and normalized to exposure or gain where metadata permits.
**Peak intensity** (fit amplitude and maximum voxel).
**Background** level and noise (local shell or annulus; mean, median, SD).
**Signal-to-background ratio (SBR)** and **signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)**.
**Lateral asymmetry / ellipticity**: FWHM ratio (minor/major), plus XY orientation angle.
**Axial asymmetry**: skewness of the axial profile, and the ratio of intensity above vs. below focus (indicator of spherical aberration or RI mismatch).
**Fit quality**: R², reduced χ², and parameter standard errors; beads below a fit-quality threshold are flagged.
**Field-dependent maps**: FWHM, intensity, and z-centroid vs. (x, y) position across the field, with a fitted plane for **stage or sample tilt** and a quadratic surface for **field curvature**.
activities: SYN-B tilt and curvature; VAL-02 tilted slide

requirement: **Field illumination uniformity**: integrated intensity vs. position (center-to-edge ratio).
activities: SYN-B tilt and curvature; VAL-02 tilted slide

requirement: **Chromatic registration** for multichannel bead data (e.g. TetraSpeck): lateral and axial centroid shifts between channels, in nm.
**Averaged empirical PSF**: sub-pixel registration and averaging of accepted beads; export as OME-TIFF with metadata, suitable for deconvolution.
activities: Averaged PSF of SYN-B ≈ ground truth (NCC ≥ 0.98); OME-TIFF round-trip

requirement: **Bead size correction**: optional correction of FWHM for finite bead diameter (quadrature subtraction or model-based), with the correction method recorded. *Implemented:* the bead is replaced by the Gaussian of equal variance (FWHM 0.527 × diameter) and subtracted in quadrature; on by default when the diameter is known.
activities: Correction formula tests; Nyquist warning tests

requirement: **Sampling check**: warn when voxel size exceeds Nyquist for the theoretical PSF.
activities: Correction formula tests; Nyquist warning tests

requirement: **Encircled or ensquared energy** (fraction of energy within a radius of 1× and 2× the theoretical FWHM).
activities: Analytic Airy encircled-energy / OTF cutoff tests

requirement: **MTF / OTF estimate** from the averaged PSF (lateral cutoff frequency vs. theoretical).
activities: Analytic Airy encircled-energy / OTF cutoff tests

requirement: The system shall compute theoretical lateral and axial FWHM from analytical approximations for **widefield**, **point-scanning confocal**, and **spinning-disk confocal** modalities, with the formula used shown in the report. The confocal models depend on pinhole size: set per channel for point scanning, and fixed by the disk (physical pinhole diameter and magnification to the disk, from the instrument profile) for spinning disk.
activities: Formula table vs. hand calculation; citation review

requirement: The system shall generate a theoretical 3D PSF at the acquisition voxel size with a scalar Gibson-Lanni model and/or a vectorial (Richards-Wolf) model, including immersion/sample RI mismatch and coverslip parameters.
The system shall report **measured/theoretical ratios** for every FWHM metric.
activities: Ratio, Strehl, and NCC tests; VAL-04

requirement: The system shall report a **Strehl ratio estimate** (normalized peak of the averaged empirical PSF relative to the theoretical PSF of equal integrated energy).
activities: Ratio, Strehl, and NCC tests; VAL-04

requirement: The system shall report a **similarity score** between the averaged empirical PSF and the theoretical PSF (e.g. normalized cross-correlation or Pearson r after alignment).
activities: Ratio, Strehl, and NCC tests; VAL-04

requirement: The system shall support user-defined **specification limits** (e.g. lateral ratio ≤ 1.2, axial ratio ≤ 1.3) and report pass/fail.
The system shall show side-by-side XY, XZ, and YZ views with overlaid profiles of the empirical vs. theoretical PSF.

For configurations that use a resolution-enhancing mode (e.g. Nikon NSPARC SR, Live-SR), the system shall keep the theoretical comparison: it shall report measured/theoretical ratios against the model of the base modality (point-scanning or spinning-disk confocal) and label the result with the enhancement mode.
activities: Mode detection on the NSPARC and Live-SR golden files; ratio tests against the base-modality model

requirement: For resolution-enhancing modes based on image scanning (pixel reassignment), the system shall also compute a theoretical PSF from an image-scanning-microscopy model and report ratios against it.
activities: Image-scanning model FWHM vs. published reassignment factors; VAL-04 on NSPARC and Live-SR stacks

requirement: For **multiphoton** (two-photon) configurations, the system shall compute the theoretical FWHM from the **excitation** wavelength with a two-photon model (squared excitation PSF, non-descanned detection, no pinhole), with citations, and shall refuse to compute it when the excitation wavelength is unknown.
activities: Two-photon FWHM vs. hand calculation from Zipfel et al. (2003); refusal without excitation wavelength; citation review; VAL-04 on a multiphoton bead stack

requirement: The system shall persist all per-bead and per-field results, the analysis parameters, the software version, and provenance in a local database.

The system shall key results by **instrument → objective → channel (or wavelength) → modality**, with the acquisition date taken from the file's metadata (falling back to the file-system date only when the metadata has none; dates in file names are never used).
The system shall plot **Levey-Jennings charts** for any tracked metric: session values over time with the mean and ±1, ±2, ±3 SD lines.
The system shall establish control limits from a user-selected **baseline period** (default: first N = 20 valid sessions; configurable) or from user-entered target mean and SD.
activities: Baseline and Westgard table tests; LJ-SIM; VAL-05

requirement: The system shall evaluate **Westgard rules** (1₂ₛ warning; 1₃ₛ, 2₂ₛ, R₄ₛ, 4₁ₛ, 10ₓ rejection) per metric, with configurable rule sets per metric.
activities: Baseline and Westgard table tests; LJ-SIM; VAL-05

requirement: The system shall let the user **re-baseline** after documented events (service, objective replacement, laser change). Events shall be annotated on charts and preserved in history.
activities: Event, re-baseline, and exclusion audit tests

requirement: The system shall let the user exclude a session from statistics with a recorded reason, without deleting it.
activities: Event, re-baseline, and exclusion audit tests

requirement: The system shall show specification limits (THE-06) together with statistical limits on the LJ chart.
The system shall provide a trend summary (e.g. slope over the last N sessions) to detect gradual drift.
The system shall support database backup and export or import, to move results between machines.

The system shall generate a **session report** (one acquisition): metadata, bead overview (MIP with accepted and rejected beads marked), metric summary tables, per-bead tables, orthogonal views, profile fits, theoretical comparison, field maps, and pass/fail status.
The system shall generate a **trend report** (one instrument or configuration over a date range): LJ charts, rule violations, events, and a summary table.
Reports shall be available as **HTML** (self-contained, one file) and **PDF**.
Raw results shall be exportable as **CSV** and **XLSX**, and the averaged PSF as **OME-TIFF**.
Output shall follow a configurable **folder and filename template** (e.g. `{root}/{instrument}/{objective}/{YYYY}/{YYYY-MM-DD}_{channel}_report.pdf`).
Each report shall include provenance: software version, analysis parameters, source file name and hash, date of analysis, and operator.
Reports shall carry a clear overall status (PASS / WARNING / FAIL) derived from the spec limits and Westgard rules.
Users or facilities shall be able to customize report branding (logo, facility name, footer) through templates.
The system shall provide a **CLI** to run analysis, update the database, and generate reports headlessly.
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall support **watch-folder ingestion**: process new files in configured folders, assign them to an instrument profile by folder or filename pattern, and skip files already processed (by hash).
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall support **scheduled jobs** (daily, weekly, monthly, or cron expression) for ingestion and for trend-report generation, through the built-in scheduler or OS schedulers calling the CLI.
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall log every scheduled run (start, end, files processed, errors) and write a run summary file. Failures shall not stop the processing of other files.
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall take all automation settings from a version-controllable **config file** (YAML or TOML), validated on load with clear error messages.
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall write a flag or status file (e.g. `ALERT.txt` or a JSON status) to the output folder when a run produces FAIL or Westgard rejection results, so downstream tools can notify staff.
activities: CLI scenarios; watch-folder and scheduler soak; alert test

requirement: The system shall support a scheduled **database backup** to a configured (network) folder, verified by checksum, with old backups kept according to a retention setting.
activities: Backup checksum and retention tests; restore drill

requirement: The system shall provide a **napari dock widget** to load a file, set or override metadata, run detection, review accepted and rejected beads in 3D, view metrics, and generate a report.
The GUI shall provide a **tracking view** to browse instruments and configurations and display LJ charts interactively.
The GUI shall provide an editor for instrument profiles and spec limits.
Long-running operations shall show progress and shall not freeze the UI (worker threads).
A documented **Python API** shall expose all core functions.
activities: API docs review; API usage tests

requirement: **Accuracy:** on synthetic Gaussian or theoretical PSFs sampled at or above Nyquist with SNR ≥ 20, the per-bead FWHM bias shall be ≤ 1%, and the error of the median FWHM of a field of 10 beads shall be ≤ 3% (mean) and ≤ 5% (95th percentile). *Amended 2026-11-13:* the original target applied the 3%/5% limits to single beads, which photon noise rules out at SNR 20; the field median is the value that is tracked. Per-bead precision is published in `docs/validation/fitting_accuracy.md`.
**Agreement:** on reference bead datasets, FWHM results shall agree with an established tool (MetroloJ_QC and/or PSFj) within 5% or within the inter-bead SD, whichever is larger.
**Reproducibility:** re-analysis of the same file with the same parameters and version shall give bit-identical results.
**Performance:** a 1024×1024×100 single-channel field with about 50 beads shall be analyzed in under 60 s on a 4-core, 16 GB workstation (excluding the vectorial PSF model).
**Platforms:** Windows 10/11, macOS (latest two versions), and Linux.
**Robustness:** corrupt or unsupported files produce a clear error and do not crash batch runs.
**Data integrity:** the database is never silently modified. Exclusions and re-baselines are append-only and audited, with user and time recorded.
**Usability:** a new user can complete a session analysis from the GUI in 10 minutes or less using the quick-start guide.
**Maintainability:** ≥ 85% line coverage on the core package, typed public API, and documented modules.
activities: Coverage report (CI gate ≥ 85%) and docs review

requirement: **Licensing:** all dependencies are compatible with distribution under the repository's MIT license. GPL dependencies are flagged before adoption.

**Deployment:** the tool runs on each acquisition PC with its own local results database. Only reports, exports, status files, and backups are written to network folders; the database itself shall not be placed on a network share. Scheduled analysis shall run at reduced process priority so that it does not disturb acquisition.
activities: Deployment review; check that a database path on a network share is refused or warned about; priority setting test

requirement: **Attributable records:** every recorded session, event, exclusion, inclusion, report, and approval shall carry the identity of the person (or, for scheduled runs, the service account and host) and a UTC time stamp from the system clock.
activities: Identity and UTC time on every record type; scheduled-run identity test

requirement: **Review and approval:** a session or trend report shall be able to be reviewed and approved or rejected by a named person with the meaning of the signature and an optional comment. Approvals are stored append-only in the database and in the audit trail; an approved report file is never regenerated in place, and a re-issued report gets a new version number that refers to the one it replaces.
activities: Approval round trip; append-only enforcement on approvals; re-issue versioning; VAL-07

requirement: **Configuration control:** every result and run shall record the software version, the analysis settings, and the SHA-256 of the instrument profile and automation configuration used, so that any change to them is detectable.
activities: Profile and config hash recorded and changes detected

requirement: **Raw data linkage and retention:** each result shall keep the source file name, path, and SHA-256; reports and exports are never overwritten; backups are verified by checksum (AUT-07).
activities: Hash linkage; no-overwrite tests; backup verification

requirement: **Installation and operational qualification:** a `psfwidget selftest` command shall run a built-in verification on synthetic data with known answers, record the environment (OS, Python, package versions, host), and write an IQ/OQ record for sign-off.
activities: Self-test passes on a clean install on each OS; IQ/OQ record reviewed

requirement: **Audit trail review:** the audit trail shall be exportable for a date range as CSV and as a report for periodic review.
activities: Audit export for a date range

requirement: **Validation records:** the validation plan, requirements, traceability matrix, test records, and validation summary report shall be kept under version control and released with each version (see `docs/VV_PLAN.md`).
activities: Validation document set reviewed at release
